sentences.text: Jabalpur, Dated: 23/12/2021
Shri Shreyas Pandit, learned counsel for the petitioner.

Shri Sankalp Kocher, learned counsel for the respondent No.7.
1.

This petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution assails the order 06.07.2021 (Annexure P/10) passed by respondent No.2 by which the State exercising its revisional powers under Rule 5 of M.P. Panchayat (Appeal and Revision) Rules, 1995 (for brevity "Rules of 1995) has stayed the order dated 05.11.2019 by which Revisional Authority Commissioner, Sagar Division, Sagar had dismissed the revision of respondent No.7 herein thereby upholding order dated 20.05.2019 of Additional Collector, Chhatarpur dismissing the appeal of respondent No.7 thereby upholding the foundational order of suspension passed by S.D.O. (Revenue), Chhatarpur u/S. 39 of M.P. Panchayat Raj Avam Gram Swaraj Adhiniyam, 1993 (for brevity "Act of 1993) placing services of respondent No.7, then Sarpanch of Gram Panchayat, under suspension on the ground of charges having been framed against respondent No.7 for the offences punishable under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
2.

It is pertinent to point out that this Court by interim order passed on 26.07.2021 has stayed the effect and operation of order dated 06.07.2021 (Annexure P/10) passed by State Government impugned herein.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner has raised following grounds in support of challenged to the impugned order:-
(1) The revision before State Government preferred by respondent No.7 against order dated 05.11.2019 by Commissioner Sagar Division, Sagar was not maintainable.
(2) The State could not have entertained the revision without condoning the delay of more than one year in preferring the revision.

sentences.text: (3) The State could not have entertained the revision on factual dispute in view of bar contained in Rule 5(1)(b) of Rules of 1995 in the absence of any legal issue involved.

4. After having heard learned counsel for rival parties, we are of the considered view that present petition deserves to be allowed for the reasons infra:-
(a) It is not disputed at the bar that respondent No.7 while functioning as Sarpanch of Gram Panchayat Bangai was placed under suspension by prescribed authority on 23.03.2019 (Annexure P/4) on the ground of charges having been framed qua offences punishable under Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 arising out of a trap laid by Lokayukta Organization where respondent No.7 was caught red handed accepting bribe of Rs.10,000/-.

(b) Therefore, in terms of mandatory provision of Section 39(1)(a) of Act of 1993,
petitioner was rightly placed under suspension.

For ready reference and convenience,
Section 39(1)(a) of Act of 1993 is reproduced below:-

Suspension of office bearer of the Panchayat.- (1) The prescribed authority may suspend from office any office bearer- (a) against whom charges have been framed in any criminal proceedings under [Chapter V-A, VI, IX], IX-A, X, XII, Section 302, 303, 304-B, 305, 306, 312 to 318,
366-A, 366-B, 373 to 377 of Chapter XVI, Section 395 to 398, 408, 409, 458 to 460 of Chapter XVII and Chapter XVIII of the Indian Penal Code,1860 (XLV of 1860) or under any Law for the time being in force for the prevention of adulteration of food stuff and drugs, [suppression of immoral traffic in women and children, protection of civil rights and Prevention of Corruption]; or [x x x]"

sentences.text: 5 . As such the appeal and revision preferred by respondent No.7 against order of suspension was rightly dismissed by Collector and the Commissioner Sagar Division, Sagar respectively.
It is surprising to note that said suspended respondent No.7 was nominated as officiating Sarpanch by special meeting of Gram Panchayat held on 05.08.2019.
This speaks volumes about influence wielded by respondent No.7 upon Janpad Panchayat, Zila Panchayat and functionaries of the State.
Less said the better.

5.1 Not being satisfied with the decision of having been nominated as officiating Sarpanch,
respondent No.7 after more than one year preferred another revision before the Minister Incharge of Department concerned assailing his suspension.
5.2 The impugned order does not satisfy two basic requirements of law;

(i) The impugned order passed by the Minister Incharge of Department concerned failed to appreciate that said second revision was not admissible and maintainable unless the delay with which it was filed is condoned.
The respondent No.7 did not prefer any application demonstrating sufficient cause for delay; (ii) the revision does not appear to have been filed on any point of law.

sentences.text:
From the above discussion what comes out loud and clear is that the impugned order of Minister Incharge of Department concerned vide Annexure P/10 is bereft of any authority of law and thus,
suffers from jurisdictional error.

As a necessary consequence, this petition stands allowed in the following terms:-
(1) impugned order dated 06.07..2021 (Annexure P/10) is hereby quashed.
(2) The State/Revisional Authority/Minister Incharge of Department concerned or any other revisional authority are restrained from entertaining second revision by the respondent No.7 against first revisional order of Commissioner Sagar Division, Sagar dated 05.11.2019 without first condoning the delay in preferring the second revision by respondent No.7 and without first ensuring that only legal and factual dispute is involved.

Since impugned order palpably reflects colourable exercise of power to favour respondent No.7 facing charge of offence involving moral turpitude, State is saddled with cost of Rs.5,000/-, which shall be paid through digital transfer in the account of petitioner and a further amount of Rs.5,000/-
be paid to Legal Aid Services Authority of this Court for having wasted the precious time of the Court which could have been utilized for more pressing matters.
The cost as aforesaid be paid within 60 days, failing which the matter be listed as PUD for execution qua cost.

(Sheel Nagu) (Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav)
